payload.task_text:
Our university bookstore wants to understand whether student academic performance in our Applied Analytics courses has any relationship with their electronics purchasing behavior. We have a loyalty program that links student accounts to bookstore customer records, and the mapping is stored in a file called student_bookstore_registry.csv in the workspace. That file has columns for student_id and bookstore_customer_id, along with the department name.

Start by reading that registry file. Then look up enrollment information for courses with IDs 1 and 2, which are our Applied Analytics sections. For each student in the registry who is enrolled in course 1 or 2, pull their submission scores from those courses and compute their average score across all graded submissions. The registry's department column is informational context only — do not use it to filter which students are included in the analysis; every student in the registry counts if they are enrolled in course 1 or 2.

On the bookstore side, query for all orders placed by the matched customers and identify purchases of products in the Electronics and Cameras categories. Count orders of every status — pending, processing, on-hold, completed, cancelled, failed, and refunded all contribute to the spending totals; do not filter orders by their status. For each matched student, calculate their total electronics spending, number of electronics orders, and total quantity of electronics items purchased. A "matched student" is a student from the registry who is enrolled in course 1 or 2 and who has at least one purchase in the Electronics or Cameras categories; students with no such purchases are not part of the analysis.

Write a Python script called cross_reference.py that reads the registry CSV, takes the student performance data and the purchase data, matches them by student ID and bookstore customer ID, and outputs a file called matched_students.json containing records for each matched student with their name, average score, total electronics spend, order count, and item count. Run this script in the terminal.

Then write another script called correlation_analysis.py that reads matched_students.json, computes the Pearson correlation coefficient between average academic scores and total electronics spending, and also computes the average score and average spending. It should output a file called correlation_results.json with the correlation coefficient, p-value, mean score, mean spending, and a recommendation field. If the correlation is zero or positive, the recommendation should be "Expand tech product section to cater to high-performing students" and if the correlation is negative it should be "Implement student discount program to make electronics more accessible." Run this script as well.

Create an Excel workbook called Student_Purchase_Analysis.xlsx with four sheets. The first sheet should be called Student_Performance and contain columns Student_Name, Student_ID, Average_Score, and Submission_Count for all matched students. The second sheet should be called Purchase_Summary with columns Student_Name, Bookstore_Customer_ID, Total_Electronics_Spend, Electronics_Order_Count, and Electronics_Item_Count. The third sheet called Correlation_Analysis should have a summary table with rows for Metric and Value, covering Pearson_Correlation, P_Value, Mean_Academic_Score, Mean_Electronics_Spend, Number_of_Matched_Students, and Recommendation. The fourth sheet called Recommendations should have two columns, Category and Details, with at least three actionable recommendations based on the findings.

Create a PowerPoint presentation called Purchase_Behavior_Presentation.pptx with five slides. Slide 1 is a title slide with the title "Student Electronics Purchase Behavior Analysis" and subtitle "Applied Analytics Course Performance vs. Bookstore Electronics Purchases." Slide 2 should be titled "Study Overview" and describe the methodology in the notes or text body. Slide 3 should be titled "Student Performance Summary" and mention the number of matched students and the mean academic score. Slide 4 should be titled "Correlation Findings" and present the correlation coefficient and its interpretation. Slide 5 should be titled "Recommendations" and list the key recommendations.

Send an email to bookstore_manager@university.edu with the subject "Student Electronics Purchase Behavior Report" containing a summary of the key findings including the number of matched students, the correlation coefficient, and the primary recommendation. Send a separate email to academic_affairs@university.edu with the subject "Academic Performance and Electronics Purchase Correlation" that focuses on the correlation insights, the mean academic score of electronics purchasers, and whether the data suggests any concerning or encouraging patterns.

The workspace also contains an analysis_guide.md file describing the methodology and a store_config.json with the bookstore category configuration and contact emails for reference. Verify the category configuration against the bookstore's actual category data before filtering purchases.

In the Excel workbook, write all numeric values as literal numbers (do not use Excel formulas). In the PowerPoint, the correlation coefficient may be rounded to any reasonable number of decimal places.

Work in a clear sequence: first produce and run cross_reference.py, then correlation_analysis.py, then build the Excel workbook, then the PowerPoint, then send the emails. Each deliverable should be produced once, by a single step, so the final files are not overwritten.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one parallel source wave and one parallel artifact wave. Dynamically resolve the workspace; read student_bookstore_registry.csv, analysis_guide.md and store_config.json. Canvas and WooCommerce are read-only. Preserve every literal registry pair, but department never filters inclusion. Before Wave 1, the main agent retrieves the complete live WooCommerce product catalog and categories at perPage=100, writes a runtime-unique product_id -> every category-name membership map, reads it back, and passes its literal path/hash to each order owner. The category names Cameras and Electronics, not a hard-coded product-ID range, define qualifying products.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 6 explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Course owner for registry course 1. Verify course/users and assignments, call canvas_list_student_submissions(grouped=false,per_page=100,page=1) for the live assignment inventory, then issue every remaining literal page from total_pages in native-parallel batches. Retain every numeric score with literal submission row.id/user_id and obtain the complete in-course user map using full_output_path for oversized rosters. Persist one unique course JSON and return path/hash, course/assignment/page/submission/user controls.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Course owner for registry course 2 — same literal recipe, only the course identity and unique JSON path substituted.
   3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Woo order owner for registry customer group 1/4 (five bookstore_customer_id values) plus the verified product-map path/hash. For each customer paginate woo_orders_list(customer=<id>,page=1,perPage=100,status omitted) through every page and include every order status. For each line item, classify it as Cameras/Electronics from the line item's own category names first, otherwise from the verified live product_id category map; never restrict spend to a stale candidate-ID manifest. Sum literal line-item total, quantity, and count an order once when it contains any qualifying line. Return compact customer rows and page/status/line-item controls.
   4. explore 3 (enterprise-data-analyst 3): Woo order owner for registry customer group 2/4 — same literal recipe, only the five customer IDs substituted.
   5. explore 4 (enterprise-data-analyst 4): Woo order owner for registry customer group 3/4 — same literal recipe, only the five customer IDs substituted.
   6. explore 5 (enterprise-data-analyst 5): Woo order owner for registry customer group 4/4 — same literal recipe, only the five customer IDs substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent joins the twenty registry student IDs to enrollment in course 1 or 2, uses all numeric assignment submission scores across both courses to compute each enrolled student's average and count, joins names from exact in-course rosters, and then keeps only students whose mapped customer has positive qualifying spend. Compute Pearson r, two-tailed p, means and matched count on this identical population and apply the exact r>=0 versus r<0 recommendation branch. Write/run cross_reference.py -> matched_students.json and correlation_analysis.py -> correlation_results.json, read both back, and freeze included/excluded IDs with reasons. In particular, Electronics_Spend is the sum of literal order line totals classified by category, not product price, current enrollment score, or a fixed product list.

Wave 2 — start three Coder writers in parallel:

1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Student_Purchase_Analysis.xlsx with the exact four sheets, identical matched population, literal statistics, at least three evidence-based recommendations and full range read-back.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Purchase_Behavior_Presentation.pptx with exactly the five requested slides and text/title read-back. It must explicitly state the matched-student count and signed correlation coefficient.
3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the two emails. For each exact recipient/subject, paginate Sent search and read candidates, send at most once with canonical matched count/correlation and required means/recommendation, then read back.

No aggregation, audit or repair agents are allowed; final acceptance uses workbook/presentation/email external read-backs.

You are gathering RAW DATA (read-only, no writes) for a student-purchase correlation analysis. Work entirely inside workspace /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-wc-excel-ppt-email/workspace. Return your findings as exact JSON blocks in your final report so the caller can save them to files verbatim.

CONTEXT: A loyalty registry maps student_id -> bookstore_customer_id. The 20 registry pairs are:
411->34, 185->47, 196->46, 399->35, 728->23, 115->29, 208->9, 473->28, 263->31, 238->45, 785->21, 565->25, 338->18, 179->41, 202->16, 113->33, 361->43, 334->49, 330->14, 107->6.
The registry CSV (student_bookstore_registry.csv in the workspace) confirms these; read it to be sure. The customer IDs to focus on are: 6,9,14,16,18,21,23,25,28,29,31,33,34,35,41,43,45,46,47,49.

TASK 1 — CANVAS SUBMISSIONS:
Use mcp__canvas__canvas_list_student_submissions on course_id 1 and course_id 2, with student_ids = ["107","113","115","179","185","196","202","208","238","263","330","334","338","361","399","411","473","565","728","785"], per_page=100, and page through if pagination.has_more is true. IMPORTANT: if any response gets truncated (looks like a preview with an output_path instead of full JSON), reduce the student_ids batch to halves or thirds and re-query until you have complete data. For EVERY submission record with workflow_state == "graded" and a numeric score (score field like "78.00"), record: user_id, course_id, score (as number), workflow_state. Build a JSON array: [{"user_id": 107, "course_id": 1, "score": 78.0}, ...]. Do not include ungraded/unsubmitted records. This should total roughly 71 records for course 1 and 30 records for course 2.

TASK 2 — WOOCOMMERCE PRODUCTS -> CATEGORIES:
Page through mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with perPage=10 (pages 1..9; there are 82 products total) to build a complete map of product_id -> list of embedded category NAMES (from each product's "categories" array, use the "name" field, e.g. "Electronics", "Cameras", "Audio", "Speakers", "Headphones", "Watches", "TV & Home Theater", "Home Appliances"). CRITICAL: rely ONLY on the categories embedded in each product record, NOT on the separate categories endpoint. IMPORTANT: if a response is truncated/preview, use perPage=5. Also count how many products belong to category name "Electronics" and how many to "Cameras" (report those counts). Return a JSON object mapping product_id (as string key) to array of category names: {"1": ["Electronics"], "31": ["Cameras"], ...} for ALL 82 products.

TASK 3 — WOOCOMMERCE ORDERS (ALL STATUSES):
Page through mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list with perPage=10 (pages 1..15; there are 150 orders total). The customer_id filter parameter is known to be unreliable — do NOT rely on it; page through ALL orders and filter client-side. For EVERY order whose customer_id is one of the 20 customer IDs listed above, record: id, customer_id, status, and line_items as [{"product_id": N, "quantity": N, "total": "..."}] (total is the line item total string). Include orders of EVERY status (pending, processing, on-hold, completed, cancelled, failed, refunded) — do not filter by status. IMPORTANT: if a response is truncated/preview, use perPage=5. Return a JSON array: [{"id": 1, "customer_id": 6, "status": "completed", "items": [{"product_id": 2, "quantity": 1, "total": "49.99"}]}, ...]. Also report the total number of orders belonging to these 20 customers, and how many distinct customers among the 20 have at least one order.

TASK 4 — CATEGORY CONFIG VERIFICATION:
Read store_config.json in the workspace (electronics_category_ids [1,2], names ["Electronics","Cameras"]). Based on the product-embedded category data from Task 2, state explicitly: do the products whose embedded category name is "Electronics" correspond to taxonomy category id 1, and "Cameras" to id 2? List a few example product IDs for each to prove it.

DELIVERABLE FORMAT — end your report with these EXACT JSON blocks (each on its own line, valid JSON, no markdown fences around them):
SUBMISSIONS_JSON_START
[ ... ]
SUBMISSIONS_JSON_END
PRODUCTS_JSON_START
{ ... }
PRODUCTS_JSON_END
ORDERS_JSON_START
[ ... ]
ORDERS_JSON_END
Plus a short summary of counts (total products, products in Electronics, products in Cameras, total orders for the 20 customers, distinct customers with orders) and the category verification statement. Ensure all three JSON blocks are complete and parseable — they will be saved to files and consumed by a Python script.
Gather Canvas + WooCommerce raw data

Build an Excel workbook at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-wc-excel-ppt-email/workspace/Student_Purchase_Analysis.xlsx with EXACTLY four worksheets, using the mcp__excel__* tools. All numeric values must be written as literal numbers (no Excel formulas anywhere).

DATA SOURCES (already in the workspace — read them first):
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-wc-excel-ppt-email/workspace/matched_students.json — array of 19 objects, each with keys: student_id, name, bookstore_customer_id, average_score, submission_count, total_electronics_spend, electronics_order_count, electronics_item_count.
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-wc-excel-ppt-email/workspace/correlation_results.json — object with keys: correlation (-0.051213), p_value (0.835062), mean_score (72.5724), mean_spending (552.77), number_of_matched_students (19), recommendation ("Implement student discount program to make electronics more accessible.").

SHEET 1 — name "Student_Performance": columns exactly Student_Name, Student_ID, Average_Score, Submission_Count. One row per matched student (19 rows) in the same order as matched_students.json. Average_Score and Submission_Count as literal numbers (round average_score to 2 decimals, e.g. 78.0 -> 78.0; keep as number).

SHEET 2 — name "Purchase_Summary": columns exactly Student_Name, Bookstore_Customer_ID, Total_Electronics_Spend, Electronics_Order_Count, Electronics_Item_Count. One row per matched student (19 rows) in the same order as matched_students.json. All numeric columns as literal numbers.

SHEET 3 — name "Correlation_Analysis": a summary table with two columns: Metric and Value. Rows (exact labels, values as literal numbers where numeric):
  Pearson_Correlation | -0.051213
  P_Value | 0.835062
  Mean_Academic_Score | 72.5724
  Mean_Electronics_Spend | 552.77
  Number_of_Matched_Students | 19
  Recommendation | Implement student discount program to make electronics more accessible.
(Put the Metric label in column A, Value in column B, header row "Metric","Value" on row 1.)

SHEET 4 — name "Recommendations": two columns exactly Category and Details, with AT LEAST three actionable recommendation rows based on these findings (weak negative correlation r=-0.051, p=0.835 — essentially no statistically significant relationship; mean academic score 72.57; mean electronics spend $552.77). Suggested rows (feel free to refine wording but keep Category/Details structure and >=3 rows):
  Category: Pricing/Access — Details: Implement a student discount program for electronics to make purchases more accessible, given the slightly negative correlation between academic performance and spending.
  Category: Product Assortment — Details: Broaden the Electronics and Cameras assortment with mid-range options that appeal to students across all performance levels, since no strong performance-spending link exists.
  Category: Marketing — Details: Launch targeted promotions (e.g., bundle deals, loyalty points on electronics) to grow electronics category share among Applied Analytics students, regardless of grade level.
  Category: Further Research — Details: Expand the study to more courses and more semesters; the current sample (19 matched students) shows a weak, non-significant correlation (p=0.835) that warrants larger-scale confirmation.

IMPLEMENTATION STEPS:
1. mcp__excel__create_workbook with filepath = the absolute path above.
2. Rename the default sheet (likely "Sheet1") to "Student_Performance" using mcp__excel__rename_worksheet, then create worksheets "Purchase_Summary", "Correlation_Analysis", "Recommendations" with mcp__excel__create_worksheet.
3. Write data to each sheet with mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel (data = list of rows, each row a list; first row = headers). Ensure numbers are Python numbers (int/float), NOT strings, in the data arrays.
4. Optionally bold header rows with mcp__excel__format_range (not required but nice).

VERIFY: after writing, call mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata on the file to confirm the 4 sheets exist, and mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel on each sheet to confirm headers and a few rows. Report back: the absolute file path, the list of sheet names in order, the number of data rows per sheet, and confirmation that no formulas were used (all literal values). Do not create any other files.
Build Student_Purchase_Analysis.xlsx

Build a PowerPoint presentation at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-wc-excel-ppt-email/workspace/Purchase_Behavior_Presentation.pptx with EXACTLY five slides using the mcp__pptx__* tools (create_presentation, add_slide, populate_placeholder or manage_text, save_presentation). Use a clean default layout (e.g., "Title Slide" for slide 1 and "Title and Content" for the rest if such layouts exist; otherwise add slides and set titles via placeholders). Save the final file to the absolute path above with mcp__pptx__save_presentation.

CONTEXT/FACTS to use (verified analysis results):
- Number of matched students: 19
- Pearson correlation coefficient between average academic score and total electronics spend: -0.051 (round to 2-3 decimals, e.g. -0.051; you may also mention it is essentially zero/weak)
- p-value: 0.835 (not statistically significant)
- Mean academic score of matched students: 72.57
- Mean electronics spending: $552.77
- Primary recommendation (because correlation is negative): "Implement student discount program to make electronics more accessible."

SLIDE REQUIREMENTS:
1. Slide 1 — TITLE SLIDE. Title: "Student Electronics Purchase Behavior Analysis". Subtitle: "Applied Analytics Course Performance vs. Bookstore Electronics Purchases."
2. Slide 2 — titled "Study Overview". Body should describe the methodology (either in the body text or in the slide notes; put it in the body text box if possible): e.g. "Linked loyalty-program registry (student_id <-> bookstore_customer_id); pulled graded submission scores from Applied Analytics courses 1 & 2; computed per-student average score; aggregated WooCommerce orders in Electronics & Cameras categories (all order statuses included); 19 students matched with at least one electronics purchase; Pearson correlation computed between average score and total electronics spend."
3. Slide 3 — titled "Student Performance Summary". Body: mention the number of matched students (19) and the mean academic score (72.57), e.g. "19 matched students (enrolled in Applied Analytics courses with >=1 electronics purchase). Mean academic score: 72.57. Mean electronics spend: $552.77."
4. Slide 4 — titled "Correlation Findings". Body: present the correlation coefficient and its interpretation, e.g. "Pearson correlation (avg score vs. total electronics spend): r = -0.051, p = 0.835. Interpretation: essentially no linear relationship between academic performance and electronics spending; the weak negative correlation is not statistically significant."
5. Slide 5 — titled "Recommendations". Body: list the key recommendations, e.g. bullet points: "Implement a student discount program to make electronics more accessible (primary).", "Expand/curate the tech product section with options across price ranges for all students.", "Run targeted promotions/loyalty rewards on Electronics & Cameras categories.", "Conduct a larger, multi-course follow-up study to confirm findings."

IMPLEMENTATION: use mcp__pptx__create_presentation, then add slides with mcp__pptx__add_slide (setting title), populate title/subtitle/content via mcp__pptx__populate_placeholder or mcp__pptx__manage_text/add_bullet_points as appropriate for each layout. Then mcp__pptx__save_presentation with file_path = the absolute path. Then verify with mcp__pptx__get_presentation_info and mcp__pptx__extract_presentation_text (or extract_slide_text per slide) and report: the saved file path, the 5 slide titles in order, and the text present on each slide. Do not create any other files.
Build Purchase_Behavior_Presentation.pptx
